findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() -- unwrap on fallible I/O in production code
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (permission denied, missing file, symlink loop, ENOMEM) panics the thread instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return a Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or typed error enum) and use the ? operator; do not unwrap file I/O

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() -- unwrap on fallible parse in production code
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV rows (non-numeric value, empty second field, extra whitespace that parse rejects) panic the thread instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use parse().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) or similar typed error; do not unwrap

findings.problem: as u16 on parsed u32 -- lossy cast that silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 in range 65536..=4294967295 silently wraps to a wrong u16 value instead of being rejected as out of range
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange) to reject values outside the u16 range explicitly

findings.problem: parts[0] -- unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 1 comma-separated part panics via index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and handle the None case with ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine)

findings.problem: parts[1] -- unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one field (e.g. 'name,') panics via index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to destructure exactly two fields; handle missing second field via ok_or

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) -- hidden stdout I/O side effect inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: Side effects leak into the functional core; caller cannot suppress logging; output is interleaved with real stdout; function is not deterministic and not testable without capturing stdout
findings.fix: Remove println entirely. If caller needs logging, pass a logger callback or return a result that the imperative shell handles

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path) -- file I/O embedded directly in the function body
findings.failure_mode: I/O is mixed with parsing logic; the function cannot be unit-tested with in-memory data without mocking fs::read_to_string; violates pure-core / imperative-shell separation
findings.fix: Split into: (a) pure parse_metrics(lines: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and (b) load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that reads the file and delegates to the pure function

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String and pub value: u16 -- raw primitives with no domain invariants enforced at the type level
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct a Record with an empty name, negative conceptually invalid value, or inconsistent state without going through a parse boundary
findings.fix: Make fields private, add a fallible constructor Record::new(name: &str, value_str: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> that validates name is non-empty and value is in range

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocation via collect() on split with no try_reserve and no max_items cap
findings.failure_mode: Malicious or unbounded input files can cause unbounded heap allocation leading to OOM; the function has no upper bound on memory usage
findings.fix: Use split_once to avoid collecting all parts; if collecting is needed, call try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| Error::Allocation) before collecting

findings.problem: collect() into Vec<String> just to index [0] and [1] -- unnecessary intermediate allocation
findings.failure_mode: Wastes heap allocations for what is a simple two-field CSV line; each line allocates a Vec + String copies
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to get (name, value_str) directly without any intermediate allocation

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics throughput or allocation profile
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, samply, perf) for hot path analysis
no allocation tracing (tracing-fluent, criterion allocation measurement, or valgrind massif) to quantify per-line heap cost
no second-ring evidence (assembly listing or MIR) to verify bounds-check elimination or vectorization on the iteration
no CLI harness or command evidence for end-to-end metrics loading performance
no tests exist for the crate -- no test files, no #[cfg(test)] module, no behavior tests
residual_risk: The function load_metrics is a single-file, single-function crate with six production-level blockers (unwrap, unwrap, as cast, unchecked indexing x2, hidden I/O println) and zero tests. The entire function body mixes I/O with parsing, has no error taxonomy, no bounded allocation, and no performance evidence. This crate would fail strict clippy (unwrap_used, indexing_slicing, as_conversions, panic_in_result_fn) and would fail Holzman delivery gates immediately. Repair requires splitting into a pure parse layer with typed errors, removing println, replacing all unwrap/indexing with checked alternatives, and adding a test suite before any performance claims.
